Hon'ble Alok Mahra, J.
Mr. Shivam Prakash Dixit and Ms.
Gyanmati Kushwala, learned counsel
for the applicants.
2. Mr. Akshay Latwal and Mr.
Prabhat Kandpal, learned A.G.A. along
with Ms. Meenakshi Sharma and Mr.
Himanshu Sain, learned Brief Holders
for the State.
3. The present application under
Section 528 of the B.N.S.S., has been
filed seeking quashing of the charge-sheet, the summoning/cognizance
order dated 17.07.2023 passed by the
learned 1st Additional Civil
Judge/Judicial Magistrate, Haridwar,
in Complaint Case No. 818 of 2021,
whereby the applicants have been
summoned for the offences punishable
under Sections 498-A, 323, 504 and
506 of the I.P.C., and Sections 3/4 of
the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, as
well as the order dated 14.05.2026,
whereby non-bailable warrants have

UKHC010187642026
2026:UHC:9577
been issued against the applicants,
along with the entire consequential
proceedings of the aforesaid criminal
case.
4. Learned counsel for the applicants
would submit that the dispute between
the parties arises out of matrimonial
discord. Applicant no. 1 is the husband
of respondent no. 2, applicant nos. 2
and 3 are her father-in-law and
mother-in-law, respectively, and
applicant no. 4 is her sister-in-law. The
marriage between applicant no. 1 and
respondent no. 2 was solemnized on
09.09.2011 in accordance with Hindu
rites and rituals, and one male child
was born out of the said wedlock. He
would further submit that, owing to
certain matrimonial differences,
respondent no. 2 initiated criminal
proceedings against the applicants,
alleging commission of offences
punishable under Sections 498-A, 323,
504 and 506 of the I.P.C., and Sections
3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,
1961.
5. Learned counsel would further
submit that, upon completion of the
investigation, a charge-sheet was
submitted against the applicants,
pursuant to which the learned trial
court passed the
summoning/cognizance order dated
17.07.2023, requiring the applicants to
face trial for the aforesaid offences in

UKHC010187642026
2026:UHC:9577
Complaint Case No. 818 of 2021,
pending before the learned 1st
Additional Civil Judge/Judicial
Magistrate, Haridwar. He would
contend that the impugned
summoning/ cognizance order has
been passed without proper
appreciation of the material available
on record and without due application
of judicial mind.
6. Learned counsel for the applicants
would further submit that the
impugned orders suffer from manifest
illegality and that continuation of the
criminal proceedings against the
applicants would amount to an abuse
of the process of law. He would,
therefore, pray that the charge-sheet,
the summoning/cognizance order dated
17.07.2023, the order dated
14.05.2026 issuing non-bailable
warrants against the applicants, and
the entire consequential proceedings of
the aforesaid criminal case be quashed
by this Court in exercise of its inherent
jurisdiction under Section 528 of the
B.N.S.S.
7. Learned State counsel would
oppose the submissions advanced by
learned counsel for the applicants and
submit that the impugned orders have
been passed by the learned trial court
in accordance with law. He would
further submit that the grounds raised
by the applicants do not warrant

UKHC010187642026
2026:UHC:9577
interference by this Court in exercise of
its inherent jurisdiction under Section
528 of the B.N.S.S. Accordingly, he
would pray that the present application
be dismissed.
8. Having considered the submissions
advanced by learned counsel for the
applicants and learned State counsel,
and upon perusal of the material
available on record, this Court does not
find any sufficient ground to exercise
its inherent jurisdiction under Section
528 of the B.N.S.S. to quash the
charge-sheet, the impugned orders or
the consequential criminal proceedings.
Accordingly, the present application
under Section 528 of the B.N.S.S. is
dismissed.
9. No order as to costs.
 (Alok Mahra, J.)
 16.10.2026
Mamta
